newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing share market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing share market report.

text.p: Dutch shares swept higher over a broad front to close at a new all-time record in hectic Wednesday trade, with Wall Street's softer opening only briefly denting investor enthusiasm.

The AEX blue chip index finished 10.40 points or 1.21 percent higher at 871.46, an all-time intra-day high, battering through its previous closing record of 862.20 set on June 20 after spending the entire session in record territory.
Wall Street's softer opening unleashed a welter of seesaw trade in the closing half-hour, with the AEX paring some of its initial gains as the Dow Jones headed south.
But as the U.S. rallied in the closing minutes of Dutch trade the index came back with a vengeance to better an all-time intra-day high of 871.28 reached earlier in the session
Dealers said sentiment was riding high on a firmer dollar and a surging German Dax, which also closed at a new record.
Major gains in index heavyweights also pushed up the AEX.
Electronics giant Philips jumped 4.40 guilders to 140.10 after showcasing the imminent launch of its audio CD recorder.
"People are impressed with the new product," one dealer said. But another said investors were seizing on any good news as an excuse to invest.

Other major gainers included chemicals group Akzo Nobel which jumped 6.50 guilders to 263.50 on a welter of corporate news and an exit from the market of a player who had been selling heavily in recent days.
"The seller is out, so the stock is recovering, but the Remeron news and carbon fibre capacity expansion won't have done the share price any harm either," one dealer said.

Another said the foreign seller could merely be taking a breather, but added DSM also looked to be benefiting from the upturn in chemicals sentiment, earlier hit by this week's Merrill Lynch downgrade of London's ICI.

Akzo announced earlier today a string of clinical and everyday trials of its new Remeron drug had confirmed earlier indications it was more effective in treating depression than existing drugs -- including Eli Lilley's well-known Prozac.
The chemicals group also unveiled plans to step up carbon fibre production in the United States.

Unilever also picked up smartly on U.S-led buyer interest, rising 7.60 to 417.90 guilders on persistent rumours it was in the market to take over U.S breakfast cereals maker Kellogg. Kellogg has declined to comment.
One of the few stocks to buck the uptrend was KLM.
Dealers said the Dutch carrier could be facing a claim for damages from the U.S. arising from the exposure of passengers to radiation on one of its London-bound flights last month.
"Apparently there's a team of U.S. lawyers currently investigating whether the passengers concerned have a case," one dealer said.
KLM shares dipped 0.20 guilders to 60.00. The stock has staged a comeback in recent days and on Tuesday peaked at an all-time high of 61.60 guilders before settling at a close of 60.20.
